passage: Faculty note, capstone project review. Arohi's team had one main requirement: a working route planner that suggests the cheapest bus route. At Monday's check-in Arohi was fixing a crash on the login page. By Wednesday the login worked, but a slide looked crooked, so Arohi spent the afternoon on slide design. On Friday it was font sizes across the report. Each fix was real and took hours, yet nobody had run the route suggestion since the first week. Jasleen, a teammate, raised it quietly. Arohi said, 'I'll get to it after this.' On demo day the planner returned the wrong route. I asked Arohi to sit with me afterwards and list what the project was meant to do.

passage:
Thursday, 11.40 p.m.
The survey project is due tomorrow at ten. I've been at it since lunch and I thought I was being so productive.
First the chart code threw an error, so I fixed that. Then the slides looked ugly, so I redid the colours. Then the references were in three different styles, so I spent an hour making them match. Then one table overflowed the page. Fixed.
Just now I opened the assignment sheet to check the word limit. The first line says: "Main requirement: compare responses from first-years and final-years and explain the difference."
I haven't done the comparison. At all. Every fix today was just the loudest thing on my screen at that moment.
Yash texted asking if I'm done. I didn't reply. I feel sick.
Indu

qa.a: The survey project is due tomorrow at ten.

qa.a: Yash may wonder if something is wrong and feel worried, since a simple question got no reply the night before the deadline.
